topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening framing introduces the lecture subject and sets out the learning outcomes before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Discovery of oncogenes through tumor viruses and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the investigation of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional categories of cancer mutations and examine how oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, and dominant negative alleles regulate cellular proliferation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genomic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how failures in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in tumor cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations accelerates cancer development across sporadic and familial syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The closing framing concludes the lecture with recommended reading and logistics for the next session.
